programmes.d: After a positive visit by Canadian Prime Minister Stephen Harper, Joe later clashes with Transport Canada inspectors threatening to shut down the airline.
Tyler stunt flies for a visiting film crew, and Andrew breaks the news to Joe that he’s quitting to go to a bigger airline.
Joe helps out an old friend Ice Road Trucker Alex Debogorski. Scott takes a scary fall on the icy tarmac. Firebrand mechanic Chuck returns to the Buffalo hangar and immediately stirs the pot.
It’s chaos at Buffalo when the Christmas toy run to the Arctic is plagued by breakdowns and the stress pushes Kelly past her breaking point.
Electra captain Ray is forced to perform a dangerous emergency landing without one wheel when the plane’s right landing gear gets stuck.

When South Korean buyers come to Buffalo to look at a water bomber, the pressure is on mechanic Cory to get the plane ready. But a landing gear emergency puts him and chief pilot Justin in serious danger.
Justin and Cory try to hoist a CL-215 water bomber sold to a Korean company onto a cargo ship – something no one has ever attempted.
In South Korea to meet the ship carrying the water bomber Buffalo is selling, tempers flare when Cory and Justin try to get the plane off the ship and delivered to its final destination.
Electra captain Brian is brought in to finish a dangerous job to a deteriorating ice strip, and Buffalo remembers aviation legend Arnie Schreder.
Justin and Cory must land at one of the world’s most dangerous airstrips in Greenland on their way to Turkey, and Mikey goes to Denmark for the opening of Legoland’s Buffalo-themed attraction.
Joe and Mikey salvage a rare tailpiece from a lost plane wreck, and Cory and Justin fight to stay aloft during severe icing over the North Atlantic.
Iron Maiden lead singer Bruce Dickinson flies Buffalo’s planes, Mikey goes for a ride in a CF-18 fighter jet, and Justin and Cory complete their epic mission to Turkey,
Dusty connects with his inner nerd after booking Star Wars movie memorabilia along with a massive Kung Fu Panda statue.
With Todd and Tamera at the helm, Gumby's trip to a 60 year celebration ends up looking more like a funeral.
Todd and Tamera prove they are NOT superheroes when they struggle to haul Batman's cape worn by Val Kilmer.
Marc lands a Frankenstein sized Munster load from the classic TV show.

Natasha risks profit and time when signals get crossed on the dimensions of a massive radio tower, while Dwight and Tyesha fear becoming the villains after a load of super hero statues get roughed up under their watch.
A massive animatronic creature with a one-day deadline is nightmare fuel for Molly and Russell, while Tamara has dreams of a sweet payday getting an oversized wine barrel across the country.

Natasha's big rig is in question when she takes on transporting a vintage fire truck to its original home, while Molly and Russell's load filled with Hollywood memorabilia is crate filled with issues.

There's turbulence in the air when Doug attempts to haul a retired airplane fuselage with his truck, as Dwight and Tyesha double book a load of ancient artifacts and a real embalming table in Austin, Texas.
As Dwight and Tyesha tangle with an animatronic T-Rex and chop it down to size, Doug bites off more than he can chew when moving a massive backyard Pirate Ship playhouse.

Molly and Russell get boxed in by the seller of a rare arcade bowling game with his shipping demands, while Tamara's haul of movie statues to Minnesota's largest candy store heats up with a large, flame-throwing side load.
Natasha is amused by her classic bumper car haul but will the ride stay intact on her rig? Meanwhile, Tamara's mini-golf run turns south quickly when the 12 piece pick up turns into a 100 item load.
Molly and Russell discover that the "magic of movies" is just an illusion when they attempt to haul an iconic picture car for a film premiere.
The falconers of Falcon Force, a service that uses trained falcons to keep other birds away from valuable vineyards, show Mike how they do it.
Mike discovers for himself why this elite Navy unit’s motto is "The Seabees build and the Seabees fight" by building a bridge in one hour after fighting off a mock attack.
Mike tries his hand at the new sport of flyboarding, soaring 20 feet above San Diego Harbor. Then Mike samples the inventions of several inventors who think outside the box.
Mike travels to Fort Bragg, North Carolina, to train and jump with the Army’s elite aerial skydiving team, the Golden Knights.
Mike visits and performs maintenance on the Out ‘n’ About Treehouse “Treesort,” and a man who turned a decommissioned 727 airliner into his home.
Mike joins two arborists on a quest to measure the world’s largest chinkapin tree. Then Mike meets the formerly homeless Cisneros, who turned his life around by stacking rocks high on the beach.
Mike joins Chief Mammal Preparator at Chicago’s Field Museum to dissect and stuff squirrels for future generations to study. Then Mike feeds and cares for penguins in Baltimore Zoo.
Mike becomes a bicycle cabbie for a bike-taxi, moving billboard, fabrication, and advertising company. Then Mike tours the Lunchbox Museum.
Mike disguised as a 22-year-old entrepreneur sells European truffles to high-end restaurants. Then Mike travels to Mt. Vernon, Iowa, to meet a man who has been impersonating Abraham Lincoln.
Mike gears up with the gravity defying dance troop and dances vertically on Oakland’s Great Wall.
Mike helps build furniture from reclaimed wood with a team of people trying to reclaim their lives.
Mike helps the Burt family make pumpkin soap and shampoo.
Mike learns the ups and downs of drone racing. Then Mike visits an attraction where people pay to crush old cars—while driving a tank.
Mike meets the family of four doing their best to be self-sufficient, which includes raising and eating rabbits.
Mike visits a unique shopping mall that combines entrepreneurship and artistry.
A landing gear collapse right on the runway sends everyone scrambling. Everything goes wrong trying to get a frozen DC4 airborne.
A sketchy landing gear light puts David and Jeff on the spot on final approach to a far north airstrip. Buffalo’s ad hoc hockey team faces off with NHL’ers
